answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a dawn as the anchor of the cost.
